headline: Bitcoin is flat near $73,600 as money keeps leaving US bitcoin funds for a fifth day and turmoil at Nvidia rattles tech stocks.

stories.title: Money leaves US bitcoin funds for a fifth straight day
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin funds had about $300M of net outflows on Wednesday 11 November, the fifth day in a row and bigger than Tuesday's. These funds are the main way US investors buy bitcoin through a brokerage account, so steady selling removes a key source of demand.
points: Net outflow on 11 Nov was $299.90M, per SoSoValue data reported by TokenPost; Trader T's tally was $299.87M, per KuCoin.
BlackRock's IBIT lost $269.73M and Grayscale's GBTC $39.13M, while Morgan Stanley's MSBT took in $8.96M, per TokenPost.
The funds now hold $93.70B in total, per TokenPost.

stories.title: Nvidia shares fall after hours on reports its board may remove Jensen Huang
stories.summary: Nvidia's stock fell more than 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday after reports that its board is preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia has not announced a decision. Nvidia is the bellwether for AI and tech stocks, and bitcoin has recently moved with tech, so a messy leadership fight a week before Nvidia's 17 November results could spill into crypto.
points: After hours the stock fell 8.61% to $158.78, after closing the regular session 2.92% higher at $173.73, per Forbes.
Nvidia's market value has fallen more than $450B since an investigation was announced on 8 November, per CBS News.
The board has 11 directors, and a majority can remove the CEO with or without cause, per The Korea Times.
On 8 November the board said it 'has confidence in Jensen', per Nvidia.

sources.label: The Korea Times: Nvidia board meets

stories.title: Bitcoin stuck near $73,700 as a December rate hike stays priced in
stories.summary: Bitcoin has gone sideways for a day, but it is still down about 8% on the week. Futures markets keep pricing a Fed rate hike at the 9 December meeting as very likely after Tuesday's hot inflation report. Higher rates make savings and bonds pay more, which tends to pull money away from risky assets like crypto.
points: Bitcoin was about $73,710 and roughly flat over 24 hours, in a range of $73,366 to $74,695, and down about 8.27% on the week, at 04:59 UTC per crypto.news.
CME FedWatch showed 88.8% odds of a quarter-point December hike and 11.2% for a half-point hike on 10 Nov, per Investing.com via Yahoo Finance.
Funding rates are still positive, meaning traders keep adding bets on higher prices even as the price falls, per crypto.news.
Open interest in Binance's BTC-USDT contract fell from $9.4B to $7.2B since mid-October, per crypto.news.

sources.label: Yahoo Finance: Fed rate hike odds

briefs.title: Strategy shares slip after MSCI confirms 30 Nov removal
briefs.summary: Strategy (MSTR) fell 2.6% to $119.06 after hours on Wednesday after MSCI confirmed it will drop the company from its indexes after the 30 November close; index funds hold about 13M shares, per CoinCentral.

briefs.title: Crypto market bill stalls until January
briefs.summary: The CLARITY Act, the main US crypto market-structure bill, is effectively tabled until January after a 49-50 Senate vote, per Forbes.

briefs.title: Group proposes moving Ethereum's quantum-safety upgrade to 2027
briefs.summary: Ethlabs, founded by former Ethereum Foundation researchers, proposes bringing the post-quantum upgrade forward from the Foundation's 2029 target, per The Block.

briefs.title: Initia says hack losses rose to $3.27M
briefs.summary: The Initia network says about $3.27M was stolen after a cloud key was compromised, leading it to halt the chain, per CoinCentral.

briefs.title: Mercado Bitcoin crypto withdrawals still frozen after hack
briefs.summary: One of Brazil's largest crypto exchanges says cash withdrawals in reais via Pix resume next week after a $49M hack, per Cointelegraph.

briefs.title: Stablecoin supply shrinks fastest since 2022
briefs.summary: Total stablecoin supply fell about $14.2B over 30 days, the largest drop since 2022, per Glassnode data cited by KuCoin. Fewer stablecoins means less cash parked in crypto ready to buy.

briefs.title: Deutsche Bank goes live with crypto custody
briefs.summary: The bank launched custody for BTC, ETH, USDC and other assets for its clients, per KuCoin.
